VLSI foundations — from transistor to flip-flop

The textbook core (Weste & Harris, Rabaey) that every later chapter builds on. Read it once; chapters link back here.
You learnHow transistors make gates, why gates have delay, and how flip-flops store bits
Used inCh 2 (timing), Ch 3 (power), Ch 4 (sizing), Ch 7 (IR drop)
PrerequisiteOhm’s law, basic Boolean algebra
Time≈ 90 min
THEORYTransistors, gates, delay and storage≈ 100 min read · seventeen sections

F1The MOSFET: a voltage-controlled switch

A MOSFET has four terminals: gate (G), source (S), drain (D) and body. The gate voltage controls whether a conducting channel forms between source and drain. For an NMOS transistor with threshold voltage VtV_t, the classic long-channel (“square-law”) model is:

ID={0VGS<Vt(cut-off)β[(VGS−Vt) VDS−VDS22]VDS<VGS−Vt(linear)β2 (VGS−Vt)2VDS≥VGS−Vt(saturation)β=μ Cox WLI_D = \begin{cases} 0 & V_{GS} \lt V_t \quad\text{(cut-off)}\\[4pt] \beta\left[(V_{GS}-V_t)\,V_{DS} - \dfrac{V_{DS}^2}{2}\right] & V_{DS} \lt V_{GS}-V_t \quad\text{(linear)}\\[8pt] \dfrac{\beta}{2}\,(V_{GS}-V_t)^2 & V_{DS} \ge V_{GS}-V_t \quad\text{(saturation)} \end{cases} \qquad \beta = \mu\,C_{ox}\,\frac{W}{L}
  • Width WW is the designer’s knob. Doubling WW doubles β\beta and the current — this is what the X1 / X2 / X4 drive strengths in the library are.
  • PMOS is weaker. Hole mobility is roughly 2–3× lower than electron mobility, so a PMOS needs about twice the width of an NMOS to deliver the same current.
  • Short-channel reality. In a 45 nm transistor carriers hit their maximum velocity, and the current grows more slowly: ID,sat∝(VGS−Vt)αI_{D,\text{sat}} \propto (V_{GS}-V_t)^{\alpha} with α≈1.3\alpha \approx 1.3. This “alpha-power law” is the one used for IR-drop in Chapter 7.

F2The CMOS inverter and its noise margins

Connect a PMOS from VDDV_{DD} to the output and an NMOS from the output to ground, gates tied together. For any steady input exactly one of them is on, so no static current flows — the reason CMOS dominates.

Switching threshold. At Vin=Vout=VMV_{in} = V_{out} = V_M both transistors are saturated and carry the same current:

βn2(VM−Vtn)2=βp2(VDD−VM−∣Vtp∣)2    ⇒    VM=Vtn+r (VDD−∣Vtp∣)1+r,r=βp/βn\frac{\beta_n}{2}(V_M - V_{tn})^2 = \frac{\beta_p}{2}(V_{DD} - V_M - |V_{tp}|)^2 \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; V_M = \frac{V_{tn} + r\,(V_{DD} - |V_{tp}|)}{1 + r}, \qquad r = \sqrt{\beta_p/\beta_n}

With βp=βn\beta_p = \beta_n (PMOS made about 2× wider) and Vtn=∣Vtp∣V_{tn} = |V_{tp}|, VM=VDD/2V_M = V_{DD}/2: a symmetric inverter.

Noise margins. VILV_{IL} and VIHV_{IH} are the inputs where the slope is −1-1; VOHV_{OH}, VOLV_{OL} the corresponding outputs:

NML=VIL−VOL,NMH=VOH−VIHNM_L = V_{IL} - V_{OL}, \qquad NM_H = V_{OH} - V_{IH}
From the plot: VIL=0.326V_{IL} = 0.326, VOL=0.044V_{OL} = 0.044, VIH=0.574V_{IH} = 0.574, VOH=0.856V_{OH} = 0.856 V → NML=NMH=0.282NM_L = NM_H = 0.282 V, about 31 % of VDDV_{DD}. Any noise smaller than that on a wire is removed by the next gate. Because the gain exceeds 1, noise shrinks stage after stage — logic is regenerative, which is why digital circuits can be chained millions of times.

F3Static CMOS gates: how transistors make logic

Every gate in the library is built from two switch networks that share one output wire:

  • A pull-down network (PDN) of NMOS transistors between the output and GND. An NMOS conducts when its gate is 1.
  • A pull-up network (PUN) of PMOS transistors between VDD and the output. A PMOS conducts when its gate is 0.

The design rule is simple: for every input combination, exactly one network conducts. If both conducted there would be a short from VDD to GND; if neither did the output would float. Inside a network, the switch logic is equally simple:

CONNECTIONCONDUCTS WHEN…BOOLEAN MEANING
Two transistors in seriesboth are onAND
Two transistors in paralleleither is onOR

Walk through NAND2 one input combination at a time. The PDN is two NMOS in series, so it pulls the output low only when A = 1 and B = 1. The PUN is two PMOS in parallel, so it pulls high when A = 0 or B = 0:

A BNMOS A · NMOS BPDN (series)PMOS A · PMOS BPUN (parallel)Y
0 0off · offopenon · onconducts1
0 1off · onopenon · offconducts1
1 0on · offopenoff · onconducts1
1 1on · onconductsoff · offopen0

In every row exactly one network conducts — that is Y=A⋅B‾Y = \overline{A\cdot B}. The same recipe builds any gate of the form Y=f‾Y = \overline{f}:

  1. Write ff using AND and OR.
  2. Build the PDN so it conducts when f=1f = 1: AND → series, OR → parallel.
  3. Build the PUN as the dual: swap every series for parallel and vice versa. De Morgan’s law guarantees it conducts exactly when f=0f = 0.
Example — AOI21, Y=A⋅B+C‾Y = \overline{A\cdot B + C}: PDN = (NMOS A in series with NMOS B) in parallel with NMOS C. PUN = (PMOS A in parallel with PMOS B) in series with PMOS C. Six transistors, one stage of delay. Building the same function from a NAND and a NOR would need two stages and eight transistors — which is why libraries include complex cells like AOI and OAI.

Why every CMOS gate inverts. NMOS transistors pass a clean 0 but a degraded 1 (Section F11), and PMOS the opposite. So NMOS must sit next to GND and PMOS next to VDD. Inputs at 1 turn NMOS on and pull the output down: a single static CMOS stage can only make inverting functions. An AND2 cell in the library is really a NAND2 followed by an inverter.

F4aSizing a gate for equal drive — and what “logical effort” means

To compare gates fairly we size each one so its output is exactly as strong as a reference inverter’s. Three simple facts are all we need:

  1. A transistor’s on-resistance is inversely proportional to its width: a unit-width NMOS has resistance RR; width 2 has R/2R/2.
  2. A PMOS conducts about half as well (holes are slower than electrons), so it needs width 2 to reach resistance RR.
  3. Resistances in series add; a gate’s input capacitance is proportional to the total width of the transistors that input connects to (call one unit of width one unit of capacitance CC).

Now work out each gate in the figure:

  • Inverter. NMOS width 1 (resistance RR), PMOS width 2 (resistance RR). The input connects to both gates: input capacitance =1+2=3= 1 + 2 = 3 units.
  • NAND2. The two NMOS are in series, so their resistances add. To total RR, each must be R/2R/2 → width 2. The PMOS are in parallel, but the worst case is when only one of them is on, so each PMOS alone must reach RR → width 2. Input A touches one NMOS (2) and one PMOS (2): input capacitance =4= 4 units.
  • NOR2. Now the PMOS are in series: each must be R/2R/2 → width 4. The NMOS are in parallel, worst case one on → width 1 each. Input capacitance =1+4=5= 1 + 4 = 5 units.

All three gates now drive their output equally hard, but they demand different amounts of input capacitance from whatever drives them. That ratio is the logical effort:

g  =  input capacitance of the gateinput capacitance of an inverter with the same output current⇒ginv=33=1,gNAND2=43,gNOR2=53g \;=\; \frac{\text{input capacitance of the gate}}{\text{input capacitance of an inverter with the same output current}} \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad g_{\text{inv}} = \tfrac33 = 1,\quad g_{\text{NAND2}} = \tfrac43,\quad g_{\text{NOR2}} = \tfrac53

In plain words: logical effort is the price of computing. An inverter only inverts; a NAND2 also computes an AND, and the series transistors that do it cost 33 % more input capacitance for the same output strength. A NOR2 costs 67 % more, because it stacks the weak PMOS.

The same counting gives the parasitic delay pp: the capacitance a gate must charge on its own output (the drain areas of the transistors touching it), relative to an inverter. Inverter: 1+2=31 + 2 = 3 units → p=1p = 1. NAND2: PMOS 2+22 + 2 plus the top NMOS 22 = 6 units → p=6/3=2p = 6/3 = 2. NOR2: PMOS 44 plus NMOS 1+11 + 1 = 6 → p=2p = 2. Generalising to nn inputs:

GATELOGICAL EFFORT g (per input)PARASITIC DELAY pWHY
Inverter11the reference
NANDnn(n+2)/3(n+2)/3nnnn NMOS in series, each width nn
NORnn(2n+1)/3(2n+1)/3nnnn PMOS in series, each width 2n2n
2:1 multiplexer24transmission-gate structure
XOR2 / XNOR244needs both true and complemented inputs

Two lessons follow immediately: wide NOR gates are expensive (gNOR4=3g_{\text{NOR4}} = 3), and wide gates of any kind have large pp. Libraries stop at 3–4 inputs for exactly this reason.

F4bThe delay of one gate: d=g h+pd = g\,h + p

Measure time in units of τ\tau: the delay of an ideal inverter driving one identical inverter, ignoring its own parasitics. Since the inverter’s resistance RR drives 3 units of capacitance, τ=3RC\tau = 3RC — about 3–5 ps in a 45 nm process.

Deriving the formula. Take a gate whose input capacitance is CinC_{\text{in}}. An inverter with the same drive strength would have input capacitance Cin/gC_{\text{in}}/g, i.e. it would be Cin/(3g)C_{\text{in}}/(3g) times a unit inverter, so its resistance is

Rgate=RCin/(3g)=3gRCinR_{\text{gate}} = \frac{R}{C_{\text{in}}/(3g)} = \frac{3gR}{C_{\text{in}}}

This resistance charges the load CoutC_{\text{out}}, and also the gate’s own parasitic capacitance (which gives the pp term):

delay=Rgate Cout+p τ=3RC⋅g CoutCin+p τ⟹ d=g h+p ,h=CoutCin\text{delay} = R_{\text{gate}}\,C_{\text{out}} + p\,\tau = 3RC\cdot g\,\frac{C_{\text{out}}}{C_{\text{in}}} + p\,\tau \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \boxed{\,d = g\,h + p\,}, \qquad h = \frac{C_{\text{out}}}{C_{\text{in}}}

Each symbol has a physical meaning you can point at:

SYMBOLNAMEWHAT IT MEASURESWHO SETS IT
gglogical efforthow much harder this gate type is to drive than an inverterthe gate’s function and topology
hhelectrical effort (fan-out)how much bigger the load is than the gate’s own inputthe size you choose for the gate and what it drives
f=ghf = g hstage effortthe part of delay that depends on load — “how hard the gate is working”both
ppparasitic delaythe fixed delay of charging its own output, even with no loadthe gate type (not its size: bigger gates have proportionally bigger drain caps and lower resistance)
Worked example. A NAND2 drives four identical NAND2 gates. Each load has the same input capacitance as the driver, so h=4h = 4:
d=43×4+2=7.33 τd = \tfrac43\times4 + 2 = 7.33\,\tau. Compare the FO4 inverter: d=1×4+1=5 τd = 1\times4 + 1 = 5\,\tau. The NAND2 is about 47 % slower at the same fan-out. With τ≈4\tau \approx 4 ps that is 29 ps vs 20 ps.

F4cFrom one gate to a whole path: GG, BB, HH, FF and DD

Real timing paths are chains of gates. Suppose the path has NN stages. Its delay is simply the sum of the stage delays:

D=∑i=1N(gi hi+pi)D = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl(g_i\,h_i + p_i\bigr)

The gig_i and pip_i are fixed by which gates the logic needs. The hih_i depend on how big you make each gate — and that is the design question: given the first gate’s input capacitance and the final load, how big should the gates in between be? Four quantities answer it. Each one is a “whole-path” version of a single-gate idea.

1 · Path logical effort GG
G=∏i=1NgiG = \prod_{i=1}^{N} g_i

The product of the gates’ logical efforts: how much harder the path’s logic makes the job compared with a chain of plain inverters (for which G=1G = 1). Inverters, NAND2, NOR2, inverter gives G=1⋅43⋅53⋅1=209≈2.2G = 1\cdot\tfrac43\cdot\tfrac53\cdot1 = \tfrac{20}{9} \approx 2.2.

2 · Path electrical effort HH
H=CloadCinH = \frac{C_{\text{load}}}{C_{\text{in}}}

The final load divided by the input capacitance of the first gate. It is the total current amplification the path must provide. A small gate driving a long, heavily loaded wire has a large HH.

3 · Branching effort BB

Often a gate’s output drives not only the next gate on the path but also other gates that are not on this path (off-path loads). The on-path stage must supply current to all of them:

bi=Con-path+Coff-pathCon-path,B=∏i=1Nbib_i = \frac{C_{\text{on-path}} + C_{\text{off-path}}}{C_{\text{on-path}}}, \qquad B = \prod_{i=1}^{N} b_i

With no side loads b=1b = 1. With the two equal side loads in the figure b=3b = 3: the path must work three times harder at that node.

4 · Path effort FF — the key fact
F=G B HF = G\,B\,H

Here is why this product matters. The electrical effort of stage ii is hi=Cout,i/Cin,ih_i = C_{\text{out},i}/C_{\text{in},i}, and stage ii’s output load is the next stage’s input times its branching, Cout,i=bi Cin,i+1C_{\text{out},i} = b_i\,C_{\text{in},i+1}. Multiply all the hih_i together and watch the intermediate sizes cancel:

∏i=1Nhi=b1Cin,2Cin,1⋅b2Cin,3Cin,2⋯CloadCin,N=(∏bi)CloadCin,1=B H\prod_{i=1}^{N} h_i = \frac{b_1 C_{\text{in},2}}{C_{\text{in},1}}\cdot\frac{b_2 C_{\text{in},3}}{C_{\text{in},2}}\cdots\frac{C_{\text{load}}}{C_{\text{in},N}} = \Bigl(\prod b_i\Bigr)\frac{C_{\text{load}}}{C_{\text{in},1}} = B\,H

Every Cin,2,…,Cin,NC_{\text{in},2}, \dots, C_{\text{in},N} appears once on top and once underneath. Therefore

∏i=1Nfi=∏i=1Ngihi=G B H=F\prod_{i=1}^{N} f_i = \prod_{i=1}^{N} g_i h_i = G\,B\,H = F

The product of the stage efforts is the same no matter how you size the gates. Sizing only decides how that fixed product is shared between the stages.

5 · Why sharing it equally is best

We want to minimise the sum f1+f2+⋯+fNf_1 + f_2 + \dots + f_N while their product is fixed at FF. The arithmetic–geometric mean inequality says that for positive numbers

f1+f2+⋯+fNN  ≥  (f1f2⋯fN)1/N=F1/N\frac{f_1 + f_2 + \dots + f_N}{N} \;\ge\; \bigl(f_1 f_2 \cdots f_N\bigr)^{1/N} = F^{1/N}

with equality only when all the fif_i are equal. So the smallest possible sum is NF1/NN F^{1/N}, reached when every stage carries the same effort

f^=F1/N,Dmin⁡=N F1/N+P,P=∑pi\hat f = F^{1/N}, \qquad D_{\min} = N\,F^{1/N} + P, \qquad P = \sum p_i

Intuition: it is like a bicycle with several gears in series that must give a fixed total ratio. Putting all the ratio in one gear makes that gear work extremely hard; spreading it evenly keeps every gear in its comfortable range.

6 · Sizing the gates: work backwards from the load

Once f^\hat f is known, every stage must have gihi=f^g_i h_i = \hat f, i.e. hi=f^/gih_i = \hat f / g_i. Start at the load and compute each gate’s input capacitance in turn:

Cin,i=gi Cout,if^C_{\text{in},i} = \frac{g_i \, C_{\text{out},i}}{\hat f}
Full worked example — INV → NAND2 → NOR2 → INV, first input 10 fF, final load 120 fF, no branching.
Step 1: G=20/9G = 20/9, B=1B = 1, H=120/10=12H = 120/10 = 12 → F=26.7F = 26.7.
Step 2: f^=26.71/4=2.27\hat f = 26.7^{1/4} = 2.27. P=1+2+2+1=6P = 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 6. Dmin⁡=4×2.27+6=15.1 τD_{\min} = 4\times2.27 + 6 = 15.1\,\tau.
Step 3 — sizes, backwards:
STAGEGATEgCout (fF)Cin = g·Cout/f̂ (fF)h = Cout/Cind = gh + p
4INV112052.92.273.27
3NOR25/352.938.81.364.27
2NAND24/338.822.81.704.27
1INV122.810.0 ✓2.273.27

The last line comes back to the given 10 fF — a built-in check that the arithmetic is right. Total 15.1 τ.

Compare a naive sizing: make every gate the same size as the first (10 fF). Then stages 1–3 have h=1h = 1 and the last inverter has h=12h = 12: d=(1+1)+(43+2)+(53+2)+(12+1)=22.0 τd = (1+1) + (\tfrac43+2) + (\tfrac53+2) + (12+1) = 22.0\,\tau — 46 % slower, because the last stage is overworked while the first three idle.
7 · How many stages?

Adding inverters (or buffers) changes NN but not FF (an inverter has g=1g = 1). Section F10 shows the delay is minimised when each stage’s effort is about 3.6–4, so the best number of stages is roughly

N^≈log⁡4F\hat N \approx \log_4 F

For F=26.7F = 26.7, log⁡426.7=2.4\log_4 26.7 = 2.4: four stages is a little more than needed but close to optimal. For a gate driving a 1 pF bus from a 2 fF input (F=500F = 500), N^≈4.5\hat N \approx 4.5 — insert a chain of 4–5 buffers. This is exactly what RC and optDesign do when they add buffers to a high-fan-out net.

8 · Try it yourself

Pick the gates on a path, the electrical effort and the branching. The calculator follows the eight steps above and also shows the naive “all gates equal” delay for comparison.

Limits of the model. Logical effort assumes equal rise/fall delays, ignores input slope and treats wires as part of the load. The Liberty tables (Chapter 2, D6) capture all of those. Logical effort is the tool for understanding and quick hand estimates; the synthesis tool does the exact version.

F5Storing a bit: latches and flip-flops

A latch is level-sensitive: while its enable is active the output follows the input (transparent); otherwise it holds. A flip-flop is edge-triggered and is built from two latches with opposite enables:

  • Setup time exists because D must propagate through the master’s internal loop before it closes at the edge.
  • Hold time exists because the master needs a moment after the edge to cut D off completely.
  • Clock-to-Q tcqt_{cq} is the slave’s delay after it opens. All three numbers are stored in the Liberty file for each flop.

F6Metastability — when setup/hold is violated anyway

If D changes inside the setup/hold window the flop’s internal node can balance near VMV_M. The cross-coupled inverters then amplify the tiny difference ΔV0\Delta V_0 exponentially with time constant τ\tau:

ΔV(t)=ΔV0 et/τ\Delta V(t) = \Delta V_0\, e^{t/\tau}

Resolution therefore takes an unbounded but exponentially unlikely time. For a synchroniser with clock frequency fcf_c, data change rate fdf_d, and trt_r of resolution time allowed:

MTBF=e tr/τT0 fc fd\text{MTBF} = \frac{e^{\,t_r/\tau}}{T_0\, f_c\, f_d}
Numbers: with tr=0.5t_r = 0.5 ns, MTBF ≈ 3.6×1063.6\times10^6 s ≈ 42 days — a guaranteed field failure. With tr=1t_r = 1 ns, MTBF ≈ 2.5×10172.5\times10^{17} s, comparable to the age of the universe. A two-flop synchroniser gives a whole clock period to resolve, which is why every asynchronous input (including a reset release in a real chip) passes through one.

DEEP DIVE device physics and circuit-level derivations

F8MOS capacitances and the body effect

The gate is a parallel-plate capacitor: gate metal, a thin oxide of thickness toxt_{ox}, and the channel.

Cox=εoxtox,εox=3.9 ε0≈3.45×10−11 F/m,Cg≈Cox W LC_{ox} = \frac{\varepsilon_{ox}}{t_{ox}}, \qquad \varepsilon_{ox} = 3.9\,\varepsilon_0 \approx 3.45\times10^{-11}\,\text{F/m}, \qquad C_g \approx C_{ox}\,W\,L
Order of magnitude for an effective oxide of about 1.2 nm: Cox≈3.45×10−11/1.2×10−9≈0.029 F/m2=29 fF/μm2C_{ox} \approx 3.45\times10^{-11}/1.2\times10^{-9} \approx 0.029\,\text{F/m}^2 = 29\,\text{fF}/\mu\text{m}^2. A transistor with W=0.2 μmW = 0.2\,\mu\text{m}, L=0.045 μmL = 0.045\,\mu\text{m} has Cg≈29×0.009≈0.26 fFC_g \approx 29 \times 0.009 \approx 0.26\,\text{fF}. A NAND2 input (two such gates, one wider) is therefore around 0.5–1 fF — consistent with the pin capacitances in the Liberty file.

Besides CgC_g, every drain has a reverse-biased junction capacitance to the body. These drain capacitances form the gate’s parasitic (self-loading) capacitance — the pp term in logical effort.

Body effect. When the source sits above the body (VSB>0V_{SB} \gt 0), as for the upper NMOS in a NAND stack, the threshold rises:

Vt=Vt0+γ(2ϕF+VSB−2ϕF)V_t = V_{t0} + \gamma\left(\sqrt{2\phi_F + V_{SB}} - \sqrt{2\phi_F}\right)

with body-effect coefficient γ\gamma and Fermi potential ϕF\phi_F. Stacked transistors therefore conduct a little less than the simple model predicts: one more reason wide-fan-in NAND/NOR gates are slow and libraries rarely go beyond 4 inputs.

F9Deriving the inverter’s propagation delay

Delay is measured between 50 % points of input and output:

When the input rises, the NMOS discharges CLC_L from VDDV_{DD} to VDD/2V_{DD}/2. Its current is roughly constant at IDSATI_{DSAT} over that range, so it behaves like an equivalent resistance equal to the average of V/IV/I over the swing:

Req=1VDD/2∫VDD/2VDDVIDSAT dV=1VDD/2⋅1IDSAT⋅VDD2−VDD2/42=34 VDDIDSATR_{eq} = \frac{1}{V_{DD}/2}\int_{V_{DD}/2}^{V_{DD}} \frac{V}{I_{DSAT}}\,dV = \frac{1}{V_{DD}/2}\cdot\frac{1}{I_{DSAT}}\cdot\frac{V_{DD}^2 - V_{DD}^2/4}{2} = \frac34\,\frac{V_{DD}}{I_{DSAT}}

Discharging CLC_L through ReqR_{eq} to the 50 % point (Chapter 0, deep dive D2) gives

tpHL=ln⁡2  Req,n CL≈0.69 Req,n CL,tpLH≈0.69 Req,p CLt_{pHL} = \ln 2\; R_{eq,n}\, C_L \approx 0.69\, R_{eq,n}\, C_L, \qquad t_{pLH} \approx 0.69\, R_{eq,p}\, C_L

Split CLC_L into the inverter’s own drain capacitance CintC_{int} and the external load CextC_{ext}. Making the inverter SS times larger divides ReqR_{eq} by SS and multiplies CintC_{int} by SS:

tp=0.69 ReqS(S Cint+Cext)=tp0(1+CextS Cint),tp0=0.69 ReqCintt_p = 0.69\,\frac{R_{eq}}{S}\bigl(S\,C_{int} + C_{ext}\bigr) = t_{p0}\left(1 + \frac{C_{ext}}{S\,C_{int}}\right), \qquad t_{p0} = 0.69\,R_{eq}C_{int}

Upsizing helps only until S Cint≫CextS\,C_{int} \gg C_{ext}; after that the gate just loads itself and its own driver. That is why sizing is a chain problem (F10).

F10Driving a large load: the optimal inverter chain

To drive a large CLC_L from a small CinC_{in}, use NN inverters, each ff times larger than the previous, with fN=F=CL/Cinf^N = F = C_L/C_{in}. With γ=Cint/Cg\gamma = C_{int}/C_g (≈ 1), each stage has delay tp0(1+f/γ)t_{p0}(1 + f/\gamma) and the total is

tp(N)=N tp0(1+F1/Nγ)t_p(N) = N\,t_{p0}\left(1 + \frac{F^{1/N}}{\gamma}\right)

Differentiate with respect to NN (using ddNF1/N=−F1/Nln⁡F/N2\tfrac{d}{dN}F^{1/N} = -F^{1/N}\ln F/N^2) and set to zero:

F1/Nγ(1−ln⁡FN)+1=0    ⇒    f=e 1+γ/f\frac{F^{1/N}}{\gamma}\left(1 - \frac{\ln F}{N}\right) + 1 = 0 \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; f = e^{\,1 + \gamma/f}

For γ=0\gamma = 0 (no self-loading) the solution is f=e≈2.72f = e \approx 2.72; for the realistic γ=1\gamma = 1 it is f≈3.6f \approx 3.6. Optimum delay is very flat around it, so designers use a fan-out of about 4 per stage — the FO4 rule of thumb, derived.

F11Pass transistors and transmission gates

An NMOS used as a switch passes a strong 0 but a weak 1: it stops conducting when its source reaches VDD−VtnV_{DD} - V_{tn}.

Vout,max⁡=VDD−Vtn(VSB)e.g. 0.9−0.35=0.55 V (worse with body effect)V_{out,\max} = V_{DD} - V_{tn}(V_{SB}) \qquad\text{e.g. } 0.9 - 0.35 = 0.55\,\text{V (worse with body effect)}

A degraded 1 of 0.55 V is barely above the next inverter’s VIHV_{IH} and causes static current in it. A transmission gate (NMOS ∥ PMOS, complementary controls) passes both levels fully, which is why library multiplexers (MX2) and many flip-flop internals use transmission gates.

F12Scaling laws: Dennard and its end

Under ideal constant-field scaling by a factor κ>1\kappa \gt 1 (Dennard, 1974) every quantity changes predictably:

QUANTITYSCALES ASREASON
W,L,toxW, L, t_{ox}, wire pitch1/κ1/\kappaLithography
VDD,VtV_{DD}, V_t1/κ1/\kappaKeep the electric field constant
Capacitance C∝WL/toxC \propto WL/t_{ox}1/κ1/\kappaκ−2/κ−1\kappa^{-2}/\kappa^{-1}
Current II1/κ1/\kappaβ(V−Vt)2\beta(V-V_t)^2, β\beta constant
Gate delay CV/ICV/I1/κ1/\kappaFaster
Power per gate CV2fCV^2 f1/κ21/\kappa^2κ−1⋅κ−2⋅κ\kappa^{-1}\cdot\kappa^{-2}\cdot\kappa
Gates per areaκ2\kappa^2Area per gate κ−2\kappa^{-2}
Power density1κ2⋅κ−2\kappa^2\cdot\kappa^{-2}

Around 2005 VtV_t could no longer fall (leakage grows as e−Vt/nvTe^{-V_t/n v_T}, Chapter 3, D4), so VDDV_{DD} stopped scaling too. With VV fixed, power density grows as κ2\kappa^2: the power wall. It is why clock frequencies plateaued, why chips went multi-core, and why power analysis (Chapters 3 and 7) became a signoff item.

F13Energy metrics and the best supply voltage

The power–delay product is the energy per switching event, and the energy–delay product balances speed against energy:

PDP=Pavg tp≈12CVDD2,EDP=PDP⋅tp\text{PDP} = P_{avg}\,t_p \approx \tfrac12 C V_{DD}^2, \qquad \text{EDP} = \text{PDP}\cdot t_p

Using E∝V2E \propto V^2 and the alpha-power delay tp∝V/(V−Vt)αt_p \propto V/(V - V_t)^{\alpha}:

EDP∝V3(V−Vt)α    ⇒    ddV[3ln⁡V−αln⁡(V−Vt)]=3V−αV−Vt=0    ⇒    Vopt=3 Vt3−α\text{EDP} \propto \frac{V^3}{(V - V_t)^{\alpha}} \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \frac{d}{dV}\Bigl[3\ln V - \alpha\ln(V - V_t)\Bigr] = \frac{3}{V} - \frac{\alpha}{V - V_t} = 0 \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; V_{opt} = \frac{3\,V_t}{3 - \alpha}
Example: Vt=0.35V_t = 0.35 V, α=1.3\alpha = 1.3: Vopt=1.05/1.7≈0.62V_{opt} = 1.05/1.7 \approx 0.62 V. Running faster than that costs disproportionate energy; running slower saves little energy but loses much speed. This is the principle behind dynamic voltage–frequency scaling (DVFS) in phones and laptops.

F14Dynamic (domino) logic — a faster but fragile alternative

Static CMOS pays for its robustness with a full PMOS pull-up network, which is slow (weak, series PMOS) and loads every input. Dynamic logic replaces the whole PUN with a single clocked PMOS:

  1. Precharge (clock = 0): the PMOS charges the output node to VDD; a clocked NMOS “foot” at the bottom is off, so the PDN cannot discharge it.
  2. Evaluate (clock = 1): the PMOS turns off and the foot turns on. If the PDN’s inputs make it conduct, the node discharges to 0; otherwise it simply stays at 1 — held only by its own capacitance.

Each input now drives only an NMOS, so logical effort drops sharply (a dynamic NAND2 input is roughly 2 units of capacitance instead of 4), and there is no PMOS fighting the pull-down. Dynamic gates can be 1.5–2× faster.

The catches:

  • Monotonicity. During evaluation the output can only fall, never rise. A dynamic gate feeding another dynamic gate directly could wrongly discharge it, so each one is followed by an inverter (“domino” logic: a rising wave of outputs topples through the chain).
  • Charge sharing. If internal nodes of the PDN with capacitance CxC_x were at 0 and connect to the output node CoutC_{\text{out}} during evaluation, the charge redistributes: Vout=VDD CoutCout+CxV_{\text{out}} = V_{DD}\,\frac{C_{\text{out}}}{C_{\text{out}} + C_x} With Cx=Cout/2C_x = C_{\text{out}}/2 the output drops to 0.67 VDD0.67\,V_{DD} — possibly below the next gate’s switching threshold. A weak keeper PMOS fed back from the output tops the node up.
  • Leakage and noise. A floating node slowly leaks and is easily disturbed by crosstalk.

That is why dynamic logic lives in hand-designed, high-performance datapaths and memories, while standard-cell flows like this lab use only static CMOS: every cell is self-restoring, and the timing tools can verify it automatically.

F15Latch-based timing and time borrowing

A flip-flop pipeline forces every stage to fit inside one clock period: if one stage needs 6 ns and the next only 3 ns, the clock must still be 6 ns and 3 ns is wasted. Latches remove that rigidity.

Replace each flop with two latches on opposite clock phases (ϕ1\phi_1 transparent in the first half-period, ϕ2\phi_2 in the second) and put half of the logic between them. A latch is transparent for half a cycle: if data arrives late — while the latch is already open — it simply flows through and continues into the next half-stage. The late half-stage has borrowed time from the next one.

For two half-stages with logic delays t1t_1 and t2t_2 and a latch D-to-Q delay tdqt_{dq}, the requirement is only on their sum:

t1+t2+2 tdq  ≤  T(instead of each stage needing its own full cycle)t_1 + t_2 + 2\,t_{dq} \;\le\; T \qquad\text{(instead of each stage needing its own full cycle)}

How much one half-stage may borrow is limited by how long the next latch stays open:

tborrow  ≤  T2−tsut_{\text{borrow}} \;\le\; \frac{T}{2} - t_{su}
Example: T=10T = 10 ns, tdq=0.2t_{dq} = 0.2 ns. Half-stages of 6.0 and 3.4 ns: 6.0+3.4+0.4=9.8≤106.0 + 3.4 + 0.4 = 9.8 \le 10 ✓. The first half-stage overruns its 5 ns half-period by about 1.2 ns, well below the borrow limit of 5−tsu5 - t_{su}. With flip-flops this logic would need two 6 ns cycles.

Latch-based design also tolerates clock skew better. The cost is harder timing analysis (a path’s slack depends on how much its neighbours borrowed) and two clock phases to distribute. High-speed processors use it; standard-cell flows like this lab use edge-triggered flops for simplicity.

F16The 6T SRAM cell — memory built from two inverters

Almost every on-chip memory (caches, register files, the SRAM macros a real chip would add next to this counter) stores each bit in six transistors. Two cross-coupled inverters form a loop with two stable states, Q = 1/QB = 0 or the reverse. Two NMOS access transistors, switched by the word line (WL), connect the storage nodes to a pair of bit lines (BL, BLB).

Reading without destroying the bit

Both bit lines are precharged to VDDV_{DD}, then WL goes high. On the side storing 0, current flows from BL through the access transistor and the pull-down NMOS to ground, so BL slowly discharges. A sense amplifier detects the small difference ΔVBL\Delta V_{BL} between BL and BLB. Meanwhile the “0” node rises a little, to a value ΔV\Delta V set by the fight between the access transistor (pulling up) and the pull-down (pulling down). If ΔV\Delta V exceeds the other inverter’s switching threshold, the read flips the cell. This is a read upset. Equating the two currents (access in saturation, pull-down in its linear region):

kax2 (VDD−ΔV−Vt)2  =  kpd[(VDD−Vt) ΔV−ΔV22]\frac{k_{ax}}{2}\,\bigl(V_{DD} - \Delta V - V_t\bigr)^2 \;=\; k_{pd}\Bigl[(V_{DD}-V_t)\,\Delta V - \frac{\Delta V^2}{2}\Bigr]

The ratio β=kpd/kax\beta = k_{pd}/k_{ax} is the cell ratio. A larger β makes the pull-down win more decisively and keeps ΔV\Delta V small. Designs use β≈1.5–2.5\beta \approx 1.5\text{–}2.5.

Example: VDD=0.9V_{DD} = 0.9 V, Vt=0.35V_t = 0.35 V, β=2\beta = 2. Solving the equation gives ΔV≈0.1\Delta V \approx 0.1 V, comfortably below an inverter threshold of about 0.45 V, so the read is safe. With β=1\beta = 1, ΔV\Delta V rises to about 0.16 V, and process variation can push individual cells over the edge.
Writing — the opposite requirement

To write, drivers force one bit line to 0. The access transistor must now overpower the PMOS pull-up holding the node at 1. So the pull-up ratio kpu/kaxk_{pu}/k_{ax} must be small (weak PMOS). The sizing order that satisfies both reads and writes is pull-down>access>pull-up\text{pull-down} > \text{access} > \text{pull-up}.

How fast is a read?

The cell current IcellI_{cell} must discharge the whole bit-line capacitance CBLC_{BL} (hundreds of cells hang on it) by the sense-amplifier threshold:

tread≈CBL ΔVBLIcelle.g.100 fF×0.1 V20 μA=0.5 nst_{\text{read}} \approx \frac{C_{BL}\,\Delta V_{BL}}{I_{cell}} \qquad\text{e.g.}\quad \frac{100\,\text{fF} \times 0.1\,\text{V}}{20\,\mu\text{A}} = 0.5\,\text{ns}

This is why SRAMs use small-swing sensing: waiting for a full 0.9 V swing would take about 4.5 ns. It is also why long bit lines are split into banks. At 45 nm a 6T cell occupies roughly 0.3–0.35 µm², several times denser than a flip-flop. Memories are therefore compiled as dense macros rather than built from standard cells.

F17The ring oscillator — measuring gate delay on silicon

Connect an odd number NN of inverters in a loop. No combination of values is consistent all the way around (an odd number of inversions turns a 0 back into a 1), so the circuit can never settle. A transition races around the ring forever.

A rising edge must pass all NN stages to return inverted, then another NN stages to return to its original value. The period is two trips around the ring:

Tosc=2 N tp⇒fosc=12 N tpT_{osc} = 2\,N\,t_p \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad f_{osc} = \frac{1}{2\,N\,t_p}
Example: with τ≈4\tau \approx 4 ps (Chapter 0) an inverter driving one identical inverter has d=p+h=1+1=2d = p + h = 1 + 1 = 2, so tp≈8t_p \approx 8 ps. An 11-stage ring then oscillates at f=1/(2⋅11⋅8 ps)≈5.7f = 1/(2 \cdot 11 \cdot 8\,\text{ps}) \approx 5.7 GHz. If the measured frequency on a die is 5 % lower, that die’s gates are 5 % slower: it sits toward the slow corner.

Why foundries put them on every wafer. A frequency can be measured with a simple counter far more precisely than a single gate delay. So ring oscillators in the scribe lines and in each chip are the standard process monitors: they place each die on the SS–TT–FF spectrum of Chapter 7 and track ageing over the chip’s life. Loading each stage with three extra inverters (FO4) makes the measured tpt_p directly comparable to the logical-effort unit used in F4.

Why even rings do not oscillate. With an even NN the loop has two consistent stable states (alternating 0101… or 1010…). It behaves like a latch, not an oscillator, which is exactly how the SRAM cell of F16 (N=2N = 2) stores a bit.

Remember
  • Wider transistors = more current = faster, at the cost of input capacitance.
  • CMOS is regenerative: noise margins clean up signals every stage.
  • Delay = effort × fanout + parasitic; equal effort per stage is optimal.
  • Flip-flops are two latches; violating their window risks metastability.
? Check yourself

Q1Doubling a transistor’s width W (everything else fixed) roughly…

β = μCoxW/L, so current doubles; gate area W·L doubles too, so does Cg. That trade-off is the whole sizing problem.

Q2Why are NOR gates usually avoided in favour of NAND?

Series PMOS (already weak) must each be ~4× wider, giving gNOR2 = 5/3 vs gNAND2 = 4/3.

Q3Allowing a synchroniser 46 ps more resolution time (τ = 20 ps) multiplies its MTBF by about…

MTBF ∝ et/τ; 46/20 = 2.3 = ln 10, so ×10.

Q4In the logical-effort model, the product of all stage efforts f₁·f₂·…·f_N…

The intermediate input capacitances cancel in the product of the hi, leaving B·H; multiplying by the gi gives F = GBH.

Q5For minimum path delay, the stage efforts should be…

With the product fixed, the sum is smallest when all terms are equal (arithmetic–geometric mean inequality).

Q6A gate drives the next gate on the path plus two equal side loads. Its branching effort b is…

b = (Con + Coff)/Con = (1 + 2)/1 = 3.

T1A chip is designed at five levels of detail

You never draw transistors for a digital chip. You describe behavior, and tools refine it step by step until it becomes polygons a foundry can print. Each step adds detail and each step is checked.

LEVELWHAT EXISTSWHAT YOU CHECKCHAPTER
RTLRegisters and the logic between them, written in VerilogFunction (does it count?)1
Gate netlistReal library cells connected by netsFunction again + timing estimate2–3

GDSIIPolygons on numbered layersDRC (manufacturable?) and LVS (same circuit?)7

T2How the tools hand work to each other

Four tools, each consuming the previous one’s output plus data from the process kit (PDK):

T3Standard cells — the LEGO bricks

  • A standard-cell library is a set of pre-designed gates (NAND, NOR, flip-flops, buffers…) in several drive strengths.
  • Every cell has the same height, so cells can be lined up in rows like books on a shelf; widths differ.
  • The power rails run along the top and bottom edge of each cell, so neighbours’ rails touch automatically.

The same cell is described in four different files, each for a different tool:

VIEWCONTAINSUSED BY
Liberty .libFunction, delay tables, power tables, pin capacitanceRC, Encounter timing, power analysis
LEF .lefSize, pin shapes, blockages; tech LEF = metal layers and rulesEncounter
Verilog model .vLogic behavior (+ specify blocks for delays)Gate-level simulation
GDS .gdsThe real polygons of the layoutStream-out, DRC, LVS

T4What a PDK is

A Process Design Kit is the foundry’s package for one manufacturing process: the cell library views above, the metal-stack description, extraction models (QRC / cap tables), and the DRC/LVS rule decks. Everything in one flow must come from one PDK — a 90 nm rule deck cannot judge a 45 nm layout.

Libraries come in corners: slow (worst-case slow transistors), typical, fast. You use slow to prove the design is fast enough and fast to prove it is not too fast (hold). Chapter 7 explains why.

DEEP DIVE the numbers behind the picture

D1Units you will meet — and how they relate

Every tool report mixes units. Keep this table open the first time you read one.

QUANTITYTYPICAL UNITSCALE IN THIS LAB
Timens, psclock period T=10 ns=10 000 psT = 10\,\text{ns} = 10\,000\,\text{ps}; a gate ≈ 20–80 ps
CapacitancepF, fFa cell input ≈ 1–3 fF; set_load 0.05 = 50 fF
ResistanceΩMetal1 ≈ 0.1–1 Ω per µm of length
Lengthµm (1 dbu = 1/2000 µm)cell height ≈ 1.7 µm in gsclib045
PowermW, µW, nWthis counter ≈ µW at 100 MHz

A useful identity: 1 kΩ×1 pF=1 ns1\,\text{k}\Omega \times 1\,\text{pF} = 1\,\text{ns}. Any time you see a resistance and a capacitance, their product is a time constant — that is the root of every delay in this lab.

D2Why everything is an RC delay

A transistor that turns on behaves (to first order) like a resistor RonR_{\text{on}} charging the capacitance CC of whatever it drives. Charging a capacitor through a resistor from 0 to VDDV_{DD}:

V(t)=VDD(1−e−t/RC)V(t) = V_{DD}\left(1 - e^{-t/RC}\right)

A logic gate “switches” when its output crosses the 50 % point:

12VDD=VDD(1−e−t50/RC)  ⇒  t50=RC ln⁡2≈0.69 RC\tfrac12 V_{DD} = V_{DD}\left(1 - e^{-t_{50}/RC}\right) \;\Rightarrow\; t_{50} = RC\,\ln 2 \approx 0.69\,RC
So: a bigger driver (smaller RR) is faster; a bigger load (more fanout, longer wire → larger CC) is slower. Synthesis sizing cells (X1 → X4) and placement shortening wires are both attacks on the same R⋅CR\cdot C product.

D3Why technology nodes matter

If every dimension shrinks by a factor ss (e.g. 65 nm → 45 nm gives s≈0.69s \approx 0.69), area per cell scales as s2s^2:

A45A65≈(4565)2≈0.48\frac{A_{45}}{A_{65}} \approx \left(\frac{45}{65}\right)^2 \approx 0.48

About twice as many gates fit in the same area. That is why the VT course’s 65 nm values (ring widths, cell names) cannot simply be copied to the 45 nm kit on your VM.

Remember
  • RTL → netlist → placement → routing → GDS; verify at every level.
  • One cell, four views: .lib (timing), .lef (shape), .v (sim), .gds (polygons).
  • Never mix files from different PDKs.

Already created it? The file you made earlier is identical except for the last four lines (PDK45_TECH and GPDK090). Re-run the block: cat > overwrites the old file. If the terminal drops characters, open gedit setup_cadence.sh & and paste only the part between the two EOF lines.

Why source and not ./setup_cadence.sh? Running a script starts a child shell; its exports disappear when it exits. source runs the lines inside your shell, so the variables stay set.

  • The physical-only list (in the LEF but not the .lib) contains ANTENNA and FILL1 FILL16 FILL2 FILL32 FILL4 FILL64 FILL8. Fillers therefore come from the LEF — that is normal: they have no logic, so they have no timing.
  • Tie cells TIEHI/TIELO (the course’s 65 nm library called them TIEH/TIEL); clock cells CLKBUFX2 X3 X4 X6 X8 X12 X16 X20 and CLKINVX1 … X20; resettable flops DFFRX1, DFFRHQX1 …; scan flops SDFFRX1, SDFFRHQX1 ….

BWrite every path into one Tcl file

Every RC and Encounter script on this page starts with source scripts/lib_paths.tcl. If a path is wrong you fix it here once, not in six scripts. The file below already contains the real values for your VM; two of its entries point to files that Step 0.5 creates (libs/…).

Open the file in an editor · shellgedit scripts/lib_paths.tcl &
scripts/lib_paths.tcl · Tcl# ---------- One source of truth for library data (values verified on this VM) ----------
# Project root = the folder that contains scripts/ (works in RC and in Encounter)
set ROOT       [file normalize [file join [file dirname [info script]] ..]]

set PDK45      /home/buet/cadence/EDI/share/FoundationFlows/EXAMPLES/EDI/DESIGN/GPDK/LIBS/GPDK045
set TECH45     /home/buet/cadence/EDI/share/FoundationFlows/EXAMPLES/EDI/DESIGN/GPDK/TECH
set GPDK090    /home/buet/cadence/gpdk090_v4.6

# Liberty (.lib): cell timing + power. 477 cells each.
set LIB_SLOW   $PDK45/timing/slow.lib      ;# library gpdk045bc : 1.08 V, 125 C  (setup corner)
set LIB_TYP    $PDK45/timing/typical.lib
set LIB_FAST   $PDK45/timing/fast.lib      ;# library gpdk045wc : 1.32 V,   0 C  (hold corner)

# Generated in Step 0.5 by scripts/gpdk045_libtool.py (the kit does not ship these)
set LIB_SLOW_SCAN $ROOT/libs/slow_scan.lib      ;# slow.lib + test_cell groups (for RC DFT)
set CELL_VLOG     $ROOT/libs/gsclib045_cells.v  ;# cell Verilog models (gate-level simulation)

# LEF: ONE file holds the technology section (layers, vias, CoreSite) AND all 487 cell macros
set LEF_FILES  [list $PDK45/gsclib045.lef]

# Parasitic extraction data from the same example kit
set CAPTBL       $TECH45/capTable          ;# used by every Encounter extraction in this lab
set QRC_TECH     ""                        ;# optional: $TECH45/qrcTechFile (see Step 4.3)
set QRC_LAYERMAP $TECH45/mapFile           ;# LEF-layer -> QRC-layer map that goes with it

# GDS: the kit has NO cell GDS and NO 45 nm stream map. Step 7.5 writes the routed
# design with LEF cell abstracts, using our own map file (gpdk090 layer numbers).
set GDS_CELLS  ""
set STREAM_MAP $ROOT/scripts/gds_view.map
set DB_UNITS   2000                        ;# LEF: DATABASE MICRONS 2000

# Power-grid layers: the two TOP routing layers of gsclib045.lef (Metal1..Metal9)
set H_LAYER    Metal9                      ;# HORIZONTAL, pitch 0.33
set V_LAYER    Metal8                      ;# VERTICAL,   pitch 0.20

# Cell names (all checked against gsclib045.lef / slow.lib on this VM)
set TIE_CELLS  {TIEHI TIELO}
set FILLERS    {FILL64 FILL32 FILL16 FILL8 FILL4 FILL2 FILL1}
set CTS_BUFS   {CLKBUFX2 CLKBUFX3 CLKBUFX4 CLKBUFX6 CLKBUFX8 CLKBUFX12 CLKINVX1 CLKINVX2 CLKINVX4 CLKINVX8}

# Supply of the slow (setup) corner, used for power and rail analysis
set VDD_VOLTS  1.08

foreach f [list $LIB_SLOW $LIB_FAST [lindex $LEF_FILES 0] $CAPTBL] {
  if {![file exists $f]} { puts "**ERROR (lib_paths.tcl): file not found: $f" }
}
puts "lib_paths.tcl loaded: ROOT=$ROOT LIB_SLOW=$LIB_SLOW"
Check it · shellwc -l scripts/lib_paths.tcl            # must print 47
grep -E "^set (H_LAYER|V_LAYER|CAPTBL)" scripts/lib_paths.tcl
Why the library decision comes first

Liberty defines legal cells, timing arcs and power tables. LEF defines the physical size and pins of those same cells. QRC/cap tables model the wires. GDS holds the real polygons. All of them must come from one process kit. Mixing technologies may let one stage run, but the handoff will fail or produce meaningless results.

0.5

Generate the two library views the kit does not ship

Why this stepGate-level simulation needs a Verilog model of every cell and scan insertion needs test_cell data in the .lib; the GPDK045 example kit has neither, so you build both from slow.lib once.

Step 0.2 showed two holes in the kit, and both block a full flow:

MISSING VIEWWHO NEEDS ITWHAT THE SCRIPT BUILDS
Cell Verilog models (*.v)Every gate-level simulation: Steps 2.4, 6.4, 6.5, 7.2libs/gsclib045_cells.v — one module per cell, written from each cell’s Liberty function, ff, latch and three_state attributes, plus specify paths for every delay arc so the SDF from Encounter can annotate real delays.
test_cell groups in the .libRTL Compiler scan insertion (Step 6.3) — without them RC cannot tell that SDFFRHQX1 is the scan version of DFFRHQX1; the report counted 0 test_cell groupslibs/slow_scan.lib — an exact copy of slow.lib (same timing, same library name) with a test_cell group added to every muxed-scan flop.

The script reads the Liberty file with a small brace-aware parser, so it copes with the kit’s quirks (for example the line default_max_transition : 0.8136 has no semicolon). It runs with the system Python of CentOS 6 (2.6.6) and was tested against a Liberty file written in the same style as gsclib045.

ACreate the script

Check python and open the editor · shellcd /home/buet/cds_work/asic_lab

Paste the whole script below into gedit (or use its Download button), save with Ctrl+S, close gedit.

Open the full script (scripts/gpdk045_libtool.py, 838 lines)
scripts/gpdk045_libtool.py · Python#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: ascii -*-
# =====================================================================
#  gpdk045_libtool.py  -  builds the two library views that the GPDK045
#  example kit on this VM does not ship:
#
#    verilog : Liberty (.lib)  ->  behavioural Verilog cell models
#              (functions, flip-flops, latches, tri-states, plus
#               specify paths so an SDF file can annotate delays)
#    scan    : Liberty (.lib)  ->  copy of the .lib with a test_cell
#              group added to every muxed-scan flop (SDFF...), so
#              RTL Compiler can map flops to scan flops.
#
#  Usage (from the project root):
#    python scripts/gpdk045_libtool.py verilog <in.lib> <out.v> [cells.lef]
#    python scripts/gpdk045_libtool.py scan    <in.lib> <out.lib>
#
#  Works with Python 2.6 (CentOS 6 system python) and Python 3.
# =====================================================================
import sys
import re

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Small file helpers (latin-1 so any byte in the .lib survives)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
def read_text(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    if sys.version_info[0] >= 3:
        data = data.decode('latin-1')
    return data


def write_text(path, text):
    if sys.version_info[0] >= 3:
        text = text.encode('latin-1')
    f = open(path, 'wb')
    f.write(text)
    f.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Liberty scanner
#    parse_block() returns the statements found at depth 0 of a block:
#      ('attr',  name, value)
#      ('group', name, args, body_start, body_end, header_start)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
TOK = re.compile(r'/\*|"|\{|\}|;|\n')
BRACE = re.compile(r'/\*|"|\{|\}')
COMMENT = re.compile(r'/\*.*?\*/', re.S)
HEADER = re.compile(r'^\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\((.*)\)\s*$', re.S)


def skip_comment(text, p):
    q = text.find('*/', p + 2)
    if q < 0:
        return len(text)
    return q + 2


def skip_string(text, p):
    q = text.find('"', p + 1)
    if q < 0:
        return len(text)
    return q + 1


def match_brace(text, p):
    """text[p] == '{'  ->  index of the matching '}'."""
    depth = 0
    pos = p
    n = len(text)
    while pos < n:
        m = BRACE.search(text, pos)
        if m is None:
            break
        tok = m.group()
        q = m.start()
        if tok == '/*':
            pos = skip_comment(text, q)
        elif tok == '"':
            pos = skip_string(text, q)
        elif tok == '{':
            depth += 1
            pos = q + 1
        else:
            depth -= 1
            pos = q + 1
            if depth == 0:
                return q
    raise ValueError('unbalanced braces starting at offset %d' % p)


def top_level_colon(s):
    """Index of the first ':' that is outside quotes and parentheses."""
    depth = 0
    inq = False
    i = 0
    for ch in s:
        if ch == '"':
            inq = not inq
        elif not inq:
            if ch == '(':
                depth += 1
            elif ch == ')':
                depth -= 1
            elif ch == ':' and depth == 0:
                return i
        i += 1
    return -1


def clean_value(v):
    v = v.strip()
    if v.endswith(';'):
        v = v[:-1].strip()
    if len(v) >= 2 and v[0] == '"' and v[-1] == '"':
        v = v[1:-1]
    return v.strip()


def simple_attr_complete(s):
    """True when a line holds a whole 'name : value' with no ';' (sloppy libs)."""
    s = COMMENT.sub(' ', s).strip()
    if not s or s.endswith('\\'):
        return False
    if s.count('(') != s.count(')') or s.count('"') % 2:
        return False
    c = top_level_colon(s)
    return c > 0 and s[c + 1:].strip() != ''


def parse_block(text, start, end):
    items = []
    pos = start
    stmt = start
    while pos < end:
        m = TOK.search(text, pos, end)
        if m is None:
            break
        tok = m.group()
        p = m.start()
        if tok == '/*':
            pos = skip_comment(text, p)
            continue
        if tok == '"':
            pos = skip_string(text, p)
            continue
        if tok == '{':
            header = COMMENT.sub(' ', text[stmt:p])
            close = match_brace(text, p)
            hm = HEADER.match(header)
            if hm:
                args = hm.group(2).replace('"', '').strip()
                items.append(('group', hm.group(1), args, p + 1, close, stmt))
            pos = close + 1
            stmt = pos
            continue
        if tok == '}':
            pos = p + 1
            stmt = pos
            continue
        if tok == ';':
            add_statement(items, text[stmt:p])
            pos = p + 1
            stmt = pos
            continue
        # newline
        if simple_attr_complete(text[stmt:p]):
            add_statement(items, text[stmt:p])
            stmt = p + 1
        pos = p + 1
    return items


def add_statement(items, s):
    s = COMMENT.sub(' ', s).strip()
    if not s:
        return
    c = top_level_colon(s)
    if c > 0:
        items.append(('attr', s[:c].strip(), clean_value(s[c + 1:])))
    else:
        hm = HEADER.match(s)
        if hm:
            items.append(('cattr', hm.group(1), hm.group(2).strip()))


def attrs_of(items):
    d = {}
    for it in items:
        if it[0] == 'attr' and it[1] not in d:
            d[it[1]] = it[2]
    return d


def groups_of(items, name):
    return [it for it in items if it[0] == 'group' and it[1] == name]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Liberty boolean expression  ->  Verilog expression
#    precedence: ! and ' (highest), ^, & * space, + | (lowest)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
EXPR_TOK = re.compile(r"\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\[\]\.]*|[01]|[!'\^\*&\+\|\(\)])")


class ExprError(Exception):
    pass


def tokenize_expr(s):
    toks = []
    pos = 0
    s = s.strip()
    while pos < len(s):
        m = EXPR_TOK.match(s, pos)
        if m is None:
            if s[pos:].strip() == '':
                break
            raise ExprError('cannot parse "%s" near "%s"' % (s, s[pos:]))
        toks.append(m.group(1))
        pos = m.end()
    return toks


class ExprParser(object):
    def __init__(self, s, rename):
        self.toks = tokenize_expr(s)
        self.i = 0
        self.rename = rename
        self.names = []

    def peek(self):
        if self.i < len(self.toks):
            return self.toks[self.i]
        return None

    def take(self):
        t = self.peek()
        self.i += 1
        return t

    def parse(self):
        if not self.toks:
            raise ExprError('empty expression')
        e = self.or_expr()
        if self.peek() is not None:
            raise ExprError('unexpected "%s"' % self.peek())
        return e

    def or_expr(self):
        e = self.and_expr()
        while self.peek() in ('+', '|'):
            self.take()
            e = '(%s | %s)' % (e, self.and_expr())
        return e

    def starts_operand(self, t):
        return t is not None and (t == '(' or t == '!' or re.match(r'[A-Za-z_01]', t) is not None)

    def and_expr(self):
        e = self.xor_expr()
        while True:
            t = self.peek()
            if t in ('*', '&'):
                self.take()
                e = '(%s & %s)' % (e, self.xor_expr())
            elif self.starts_operand(t):          # implicit AND (space)
                e = '(%s & %s)' % (e, self.xor_expr())
            else:
                return e

    def xor_expr(self):
        e = self.unary()
        while self.peek() == '^':
            self.take()
            e = '(%s ^ %s)' % (e, self.unary())
        return e

    def unary(self):
        if self.peek() == '!':
            self.take()
            return '(~%s)' % self.unary()
        e = self.primary()
        while self.peek() == "'":
            self.take()
            e = '(~%s)' % e
        return e

    def primary(self):
        t = self.take()
        if t is None:
            raise ExprError('expression ends too early')
        if t == '(':
            e = self.or_expr()
            if self.take() != ')':
                raise ExprError('missing )')
            return e
        if t == '0':
            return "1'b0"
        if t == '1':
            return "1'b1"
        if re.match(r'[A-Za-z_]', t):
            name = self.rename.get(t, t)
            if name not in self.names:
                self.names.append(name)
            return vname(name)
        raise ExprError('unexpected "%s"' % t)


def lib2v(expr, rename=None):
    return ExprParser(expr, rename or {}).parse()


VERILOG_KEYWORDS = set(('always and assign begin buf bufif0 bufif1 case casex casez cmos deassign '
                        'default defparam disable edge else end endcase endfunction endmodule '
                        'endprimitive endspecify endtable endtask event for force forever fork '
                        'function highz0 highz1 if ifnone initial inout input integer join large '
                        'macromodule medium module nand negedge nmos nor not notif0 notif1 or '
                        'output parameter pmos posedge primitive pull0 pull1 pulldown pullup '
                        'rcmos real realtime reg release repeat rnmos rpmos rtran rtranif0 '
                        'rtranif1 scalared small specify specparam strong0 strong1 supply0 '
                        'supply1 table task time tran tranif0 tranif1 tri tri0 tri1 triand '
                        'trior trireg vectored wait wand weak0 weak1 while wire wor xnor xor').split())


def vname(n):
    if n in VERILOG_KEYWORDS or not re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$', n):
        return '\\' + n + ' '
    return n


def edge_of(expr):
    """'CK' -> ('posedge','CK');  '!CKN' / "CKN'" -> ('negedge','CKN'); else None."""
    s = expr.replace(' ', '')
    while s.startswith('(') and s.endswith(')'):
        s = s[1:-1]
    m = re.match(r'^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)$', s)
    if m:
        return ('posedge', m.group(1))
    m = re.match(r"^!\(?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\)?$", s) or re.match(r"^\(?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\)?'$", s)
    if m:
        return ('negedge', m.group(1))
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Library model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class Pin(object):
    def __init__(self, name, attrs, timings):
        self.name = name
        self.attrs = attrs
        self.direction = attrs.get('direction', 'input')
        self.function = attrs.get('function')
        self.three_state = attrs.get('three_state')
        self.timings = timings                   # list of attr dicts


class Cell(object):
    def __init__(self, name, start, end):
        self.name = name
        self.start = start                       # body start
        self.end = end                           # index of closing brace
        self.pins = []
        self.ff = None                           # (vars, attrs)
        self.latch = None
        self.statetable = False
        self.has_test_cell = False

    def pin(self, name):
        for p in self.pins:
            if p.name == name:
                return p
        return None


def load_library(path):
    text = read_text(path)
    top = parse_block(text, 0, len(text))
    libs = groups_of(top, 'library')
    if not libs:
        raise SystemExit('ERROR: no library() group found in %s' % path)
    lib = libs[0]
    libname = lib[2]
    lib_items = parse_block(text, lib[3], lib[4])
    cells = []
    for g in groups_of(lib_items, 'cell'):
        cell = Cell(g[2], g[3], g[4])
        citems = parse_block(text, g[3], g[4])
        for it in citems:
            if it[0] != 'group':
                continue
            gname = it[1]
            if gname == 'pin':
                pitems = parse_block(text, it[3], it[4])
                timings = []
                for t in groups_of(pitems, 'timing'):
                    timings.append(attrs_of(parse_block(text, t[3], t[4])))
                for pname in [x.strip() for x in it[2].split(',') if x.strip()]:
                    cell.pins.append(Pin(pname, attrs_of(pitems), timings))
            elif gname in ('ff', 'latch'):
                vars_ = [x.strip() for x in it[2].split(',') if x.strip()]
                gattrs = attrs_of(parse_block(text, it[3], it[4]))
                if gname == 'ff':
                    cell.ff = (vars_, gattrs)
                else:
                    cell.latch = (vars_, gattrs)
            elif gname == 'statetable':
                cell.statetable = True
            elif gname == 'test_cell':
                cell.has_test_cell = True
        cells.append(cell)
    return text, libname, cells


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  verilog mode
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
CPV = {'L': "1'b0", 'H': "1'b1", 'X': "1'bx"}


def cpv_value(v, var):
    v = (v or 'X').strip().upper()
    if v == 'N':
        return vname(var)
    if v == 'T':
        return '~' + vname(var)
    return CPV.get(v, "1'bx")


def seq_assign(vars_, value_q, value_qn, blocking):
    op = '=' if blocking else '<='
    parts = ['%s %s %s;' % (vname(vars_[0]), op, value_q)]
    if len(vars_) > 1:
        parts.append('%s %s %s;' % (vname(vars_[1]), op, value_qn))
    return 'begin ' + ' '.join(parts) + ' end'


def event_for(expr, label, lines, active_high_edge):
    """Return a sensitivity item for a clock/clear/preset expression."""
    e = edge_of(expr)
    if e is not None:
        if not active_high_edge:
            # for clear/preset the edge that ASSERTS the signal
            return '%s %s' % (e[0], vname(e[1]))
        return '%s %s' % (e[0], vname(e[1]))
    wname = 'cdn_' + label
    lines.append('  wire %s = %s;' % (wname, lib2v(expr)))
    return 'posedge ' + wname


def ff_block(cell, lines, warns):
    vars_, a = cell.ff
    ns = a.get('next_state')
    clk = a.get('clocked_on')
    if ns is None or clk is None:
        warns.append('%s: ff without next_state/clocked_on - modelled as X' % cell.name)
        return False
    lines.append('  reg %s;' % ', '.join([vname(v) for v in vars_]))
    sens = [event_for(clk, 'clk', lines, True)]
    clr = a.get('clear')
    pre = a.get('preset')
    if clr:
        sens.append(event_for(clr, 'clr', lines, False))
    if pre:
        sens.append(event_for(pre, 'pre', lines, False))
    nsv = lib2v(ns)
    lines.append('  always @(%s) begin' % ' or '.join(sens))
    first = True
    if clr and pre:
        lines.append('    if (%s && %s) %s' % (lib2v(clr), lib2v(pre), seq_assign(
            vars_, cpv_value(a.get('clear_preset_var1'), vars_[0]),
            cpv_value(a.get('clear_preset_var2'), vars_[-1]), False)))
        first = False
    if clr:
        lines.append('    %sif (%s) %s' % ('' if first else 'else ', lib2v(clr),
                                          seq_assign(vars_, "1'b0", "1'b1", False)))
        first = False
    if pre:
        lines.append('    %sif (%s) %s' % ('' if first else 'else ', lib2v(pre),
                                          seq_assign(vars_, "1'b1", "1'b0", False)))
        first = False
    body = seq_assign(vars_, nsv, '~' + nsv, False)
    if first:
        lines.append('    ' + body)
    else:
        lines.append('    else ' + body)
    lines.append('  end')
    return True


def latch_block(cell, lines, warns):
    vars_, a = cell.latch
    en = a.get('enable')
    d = a.get('data_in')
    if en is None or d is None:
        warns.append('%s: latch without enable/data_in - modelled as X' % cell.name)
        return False
    lines.append('  reg %s;' % ', '.join([vname(v) for v in vars_]))
    clr = a.get('clear')
    pre = a.get('preset')
    dv = lib2v(d)
    lines.append('  always @(*) begin')
    first = True
    if clr and pre:
        lines.append('    if (%s && %s) %s' % (lib2v(clr), lib2v(pre), seq_assign(
            vars_, cpv_value(a.get('clear_preset_var1'), vars_[0]),
            cpv_value(a.get('clear_preset_var2'), vars_[-1]), True)))
        first = False
    if clr:
        lines.append('    %sif (%s) %s' % ('' if first else 'else ', lib2v(clr),
                                          seq_assign(vars_, "1'b0", "1'b1", True)))
        first = False
    if pre:
        lines.append('    %sif (%s) %s' % ('' if first else 'else ', lib2v(pre),
                                          seq_assign(vars_, "1'b1", "1'b0", True)))
        first = False
    lines.append('    %sif (%s) %s' % ('' if first else 'else ', lib2v(en),
                                      seq_assign(vars_, dv, '~' + dv, True)))
    lines.append('  end')
    return True


SKIP_TIMING = re.compile(r'^(setup|hold|recovery|removal|skew|non_seq|nochange|min_pulse|minimum_period|max_clock)')


def specify_lines(cell, inputs, outputs):
    paths = []
    seen = set()

    def add(line):
        if line not in seen:
            seen.add(line)
            paths.append(line)

    for p in cell.pins:
        if p.name not in outputs:
            continue
        uncond = set()
        conds = {}
        for t in p.timings:
            ttype = t.get('timing_type', 'combinational')
            if SKIP_TIMING.match(ttype):
                continue
            sense = t.get('timing_sense', '')
            cond = t.get('sdf_cond')
            if not cond and t.get('when'):
                try:
                    cond = lib2v(t.get('when'))
                except ExprError:
                    cond = None
            for src in t.get('related_pin', '').replace('"', '').split():
                if src not in inputs:
                    continue
                edge = None
                if ttype == 'rising_edge':
                    edge = 'posedge'
                elif ttype == 'falling_edge':
                    edge = 'negedge'
                elif ttype == 'clear':
                    edge = {'positive_unate': 'negedge', 'negative_unate': 'posedge'}.get(sense)
                elif ttype == 'preset':
                    edge = {'positive_unate': 'posedge', 'negative_unate': 'negedge'}.get(sense)
                key = (edge, src)
                if edge:
                    core = '(%s %s => (%s : %s))' % (edge, vname(src), vname(p.name), vname(src))
                    add('    %s = (0, 0);' % core)          # always keep an unconditional edge path
                    if cond:
                        add('    if (%s) %s = (0, 0);' % (cond, core))
                else:
                    core = '(%s => %s)' % (vname(src), vname(p.name))
                    if cond:
                        conds.setdefault(key, []).append(cond)
                    else:
                        uncond.add(key)
        for key in conds:
            core = '(%s => %s)' % (vname(key[1]), vname(p.name))
            for c in conds[key]:
                add('    if (%s) %s = (0, 0);' % (c, core))
            if key not in uncond:
                add('    ifnone %s = (0, 0);' % core)
        for key in uncond:
            add('    (%s => %s) = (0, 0);' % (vname(key[1]), vname(p.name)))
    return paths


def cell_module(cell, warns, with_specify):
    ports = [p for p in cell.pins if p.direction in ('input', 'output', 'inout')]
    inputs = [p.name for p in ports if p.direction in ('input', 'inout')]
    outputs = [p.name for p in ports if p.direction in ('output', 'inout')]
    lines = []
    lines.append('`celldefine')
    lines.append('module %s (%s);' % (cell.name, ', '.join([vname(p.name) for p in ports])))
    for p in ports:
        lines.append('  %s %s;' % (p.direction, vname(p.name)))
    seq_ok = True
    seq_vars = []
    if cell.ff is not None:
        seq_vars = cell.ff[0]
    elif cell.latch is not None:
        seq_vars = cell.latch[0]
    if cell.ff is not None:
        seq_ok = ff_block(cell, lines, warns)
    elif cell.latch is not None:
        seq_ok = latch_block(cell, lines, warns)
    elif cell.statetable:
        seq_ok = False
        warns.append('%s: statetable cell - outputs modelled as X' % cell.name)
    for p in ports:
        if p.direction == 'input':
            continue
        if p.function is None:
            if p.direction == 'output':
                lines.append("  assign %s = 1'bx;  // no function in .lib" % vname(p.name))
                warns.append('%s: output %s has no function - modelled as X' % (cell.name, p.name))
            continue
        try:
            f = lib2v(p.function)
            known = set([q.name for q in ports] + seq_vars)
            used = [x for x in re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*', p.function)]
            if (not seq_ok and [x for x in used if x in seq_vars]) or [x for x in used if x not in known]:
                f = "1'bx"
                warns.append('%s: output %s depends on unmodelled state - modelled as X' % (cell.name, p.name))
            if p.three_state:
                lines.append("  assign %s = %s ? 1'bz : %s;" % (vname(p.name), lib2v(p.three_state), f))
            else:
                lines.append('  assign %s = %s;' % (vname(p.name), f))
        except ExprError:
            lines.append("  assign %s = 1'bx;  // unparsed: %s" % (vname(p.name), p.function))
            warns.append('%s: could not parse function of %s' % (cell.name, p.name))
    if with_specify:
        sp = specify_lines(cell, inputs, outputs)
        if sp:
            lines.append('  specify')
            lines.extend(sp)
            lines.append('  endspecify')
    lines.append('endmodule')
    lines.append('`endcelldefine')
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def lef_macros(path):
    """{macro: [(pin, direction), ...]} for signal pins of every LEF MACRO."""
    macros = {}
    cur = None
    pin = None
    pdir = 'INPUT'
    puse = 'SIGNAL'
    for raw in read_text(path).splitlines():
        w = raw.split()
        if not w:
            continue
        if w[0] == 'MACRO' and len(w) > 1:
            cur = w[1]
            macros[cur] = []
        elif cur and w[0] == 'PIN' and len(w) > 1:
            pin = w[1]
            pdir = 'INPUT'
            puse = 'SIGNAL'
        elif cur and pin and w[0] == 'DIRECTION' and len(w) > 1:
            pdir = w[1]
        elif cur and pin and w[0] == 'USE' and len(w) > 1:
            puse = w[1]
        elif cur and w[0] == 'END' and len(w) > 1:
            if pin and w[1] == pin:
                if puse.rstrip(';') not in ('POWER', 'GROUND'):
                    macros[cur].append((pin, pdir.rstrip(';').lower()))
                pin = None
            elif w[1] == cur:
                cur = None
    return macros


def do_verilog(lib_path, out_path, lef_path=None):
    text, libname, cells = load_library(lib_path)
    warns = []
    out = []
    out.append('// ' + '=' * 70)
    out.append('// Behavioural Verilog models generated from %s' % lib_path)
    out.append('// Library: %s   cells: %d' % (libname, len(cells)))
    out.append('// Generated by scripts/gpdk045_libtool.py - functional models with')
    out.append('// zero-delay specify paths (annotated by SDF); no timing checks.')
    out.append('// ' + '=' * 70)
    out.append('`timescale 1ns/1ps')
    out.append('')
    names = set()
    for c in cells:
        out.append(cell_module(c, warns, True))
        names.add(c.name)
    extra = 0
    if lef_path:
        for m, pins in sorted(lef_macros(lef_path).items()):
            if m in names:
                continue
            out.append('`celldefine')
            if pins:
                out.append('module %s (%s);  // physical-only LEF macro' % (m, ', '.join([vname(p[0]) for p in pins])))
            else:
                out.append('module %s;  // physical-only LEF macro (no signal pins)' % m)
            for pn, pd in pins:
                d = pd if pd in ('output', 'inout') else 'input'
                out.append('  %s %s;' % (d, vname(pn)))
            out.append('endmodule')
            out.append('`endcelldefine')
            out.append('')
            extra += 1
    write_text(out_path, '\n'.join(out) + '\n')
    nseq = len([c for c in cells if c.ff is not None])
    nlat = len([c for c in cells if c.latch is not None])
    print('verilog: library %s, %d cells read from %s' % (libname, len(cells), lib_path))
    print('verilog: %d flip-flop cells, %d latch cells, %d combinational cells'
          % (nseq, nlat, len(cells) - nseq - nlat))
    if lef_path:
        print('verilog: %d physical-only LEF macros added as empty modules' % extra)
    print('verilog: %d warnings' % len(warns))
    for w in warns[:40]:
        print('  WARNING: ' + w)
    print('verilog: wrote %s' % out_path)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  scan mode
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
QUOTED = ('next_state', 'clocked_on', 'clocked_on_also', 'clear', 'preset')
SCAN_NAME = re.compile(r'^SDFF')
SCAN_SKIP = re.compile(r'^SDFFTR')       # synchronous-reset scan flops: next_state is not just D


def test_cell_text(cell):
    vars_, a = cell.ff
    out = []
    out.append('    test_cell () {')
    for p in cell.pins:
        if p.direction != 'input':
            continue
        extra = ''
        if p.name == 'SI':
            extra = ' signal_type : test_scan_in ;'
        elif p.name == 'SE':
            extra = ' signal_type : test_scan_enable ;'
        out.append('      pin (%s) { direction : input ;%s }' % (p.name, extra))
    ffa = []
    ffa.append('next_state : "D" ;')
    for k in ('clocked_on', 'clocked_on_also', 'clear', 'preset', 'clear_preset_var1', 'clear_preset_var2'):
        if k in a:
            if k in QUOTED:
                ffa.append('%s : "%s" ;' % (k, a[k]))
            else:
                ffa.append('%s : %s ;' % (k, a[k]))
    out.append('      ff (%s) { %s }' % (','.join(vars_), ' '.join(ffa)))
    for p in cell.pins:
        if p.direction != 'output':
            continue
        f = (p.function or '').replace(' ', '').replace('(', '').replace(')', '')
        if f == vars_[0]:
            st = 'test_scan_out'
        elif len(vars_) > 1 and f == vars_[1]:
            st = 'test_scan_out_inverted'
        else:
            return None
        out.append('      pin (%s) { direction : output ; function : "%s" ; signal_type : %s ; }'
                   % (p.name, f, st))
    out.append('    }')
    return '\n'.join(out) + '\n  '


def do_scan(lib_path, out_path):
    text, libname, cells = load_library(lib_path)
    inserts = []
    done = []
    skipped = []
    for c in cells:
        if not SCAN_NAME.match(c.name):
            continue
        why = None
        if SCAN_SKIP.match(c.name):
            why = 'synchronous reset (next_state is not D)'
        elif c.has_test_cell:
            why = 'already has a test_cell'
        elif c.ff is None:
            why = 'no ff group'
        elif c.pin('SE') is None or c.pin('SI') is None or c.pin('D') is None:
            why = 'missing D/SI/SE pin'
        tc = None
        if why is None:
            tc = test_cell_text(c)
            if tc is None:
                why = 'output function is not IQ/IQN'
        if why:
            skipped.append('%s (%s)' % (c.name, why))
            continue
        # insert just before the closing brace of the cell
        q = c.end
        while q > c.start and text[q - 1] in ' \t':
            q -= 1
        inserts.append((q, tc))
        done.append(c.name)
    pieces = []
    last = 0
    for pos, t in sorted(inserts):
        pieces.append(text[last:pos])
        pieces.append(t)
        last = pos
    pieces.append(text[last:])
    new = ''.join(pieces)
    # sanity: the new file must still parse
    match_brace(new, new.index('{', new.find('library')))
    write_text(out_path, new)
    print('scan: library %s, %d cells read from %s' % (libname, len(cells), lib_path))
    print('scan: test_cell added to %d scan flops:' % len(done))
    for i in range(0, len(done), 8):
        print('   ' + ' '.join(done[i:i + 8]))
    print('scan: %d SDFF cells left unchanged:' % len(skipped))
    for s in skipped:
        print('   ' + s)
    print('scan: wrote %s' % out_path)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
def main(argv):
    if len(argv) >= 4 and argv[1] == 'verilog':
        lef = None
        if len(argv) >= 5:
            lef = argv[4]
        do_verilog(argv[2], argv[3], lef)
    elif len(argv) >= 4 and argv[1] == 'scan':
        do_scan(argv[2], argv[3])
    else:
        sys.stderr.write(__doc__ or '')
        sys.stderr.write('usage:\n  python gpdk045_libtool.py verilog <in.lib> <out.v> [cells.lef]\n'
                         '  python gpdk045_libtool.py scan    <in.lib> <out.lib>\n')
        return 2
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

  • The four SDFFTR… cells are listed as unchanged: their reset is synchronous (part of next_state), so their non-scan behaviour is not simply “D” — RC will not use them for this counter anyway.
  • The test_cell of each flop lists its pins, marks SI as test_scan_in, SE as test_scan_enable, Q as test_scan_out, and repeats the flop with next_state : "D".

DCompile the models once

Warnings about specify paths or `celldefine are harmless. -compile stops after compilation; it only proves every module parses.

Troubleshooting — the library script

SyntaxError or IndentationError — the paste lost characters. Compare wc -l with the number above; delete the file and paste again into gedit (not the terminal), or use the Download button.

ERROR: no library() group found — the first argument is not a Liberty file; check ls $PDK45/timing/slow.lib.

irun reports *E in a cell module — note the cell name from the error and send it along with the matching cell from the .lib (grep -n -A40 "cell (NAME)" $PDK45/timing/slow.lib); that cell uses a Liberty construct the script does not model yet. All cells that RC picks for this lab (DFFR*, SDFFR*, XOR/XNOR, NAND/NOR, AOI/OAI, MX2, ADDH, INV, BUF, CLKBUF, TIE*) are covered.

Do these models replace the vendor’s? No. They are functional models with zero-delay paths that SDF annotates; they carry no setup/hold checks. Timing correctness is proven by Encounter’s static timing, not by these models (Step 7.2 states this explicitly).

Why the Liberty file is enough to build simulation models

Liberty already contains each cell’s logic: function : "(!(A B))" for a NAND2, and for a flop an ff (IQ,IQN) group with next_state, clocked_on and clear. A simulation model is the same information written in Verilog. The timing arcs (related_pin, timing_type, sdf_cond) become the specify paths that SDF annotation needs.

Checkpointlibs/gsclib045_cells.v and libs/slow_scan.lib exist, the script printed ≈477 cells and ≈40 patched scan flops, and logs/irun_cells.log has 0 *E lines.
