8.1

Historical remote-access setup

Why this stepNeeded only if you ever run the tools on a remote server instead of the local VM.

The course documents Xming/PuTTY/WinSCP on Windows and XQuartz plus ssh -X on macOS, to display Linux GUI tools running on a remote server. Use your college’s current VPN and SSH guidance rather than installing the exact old versions blindly. On your VM you are already working locally, so this whole step is only needed if you ever run the tools on a remote server.

1Install and start an X server (Windows: Xming)

Install Xming with all default options, then the Xming-fonts package into the same folder (with Xming closed). Xming must be running before you connect. Check the taskbar for its icon:

…or open the Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc → Processes) and look for Xming.exe:

Today: Windows 10/11 users can instead use VcXsrv, MobaXterm (built-in X server), or WSLg.

2Connect with PuTTY and X11 forwarding

  1. Run putty.exe. In the left tree go to Connection → SSH → X11 and tick Enable X11 forwarding.
  2. Go back to Session, type the server's host name, enter a name under Saved Sessions and click Save.
  3. Select the saved session and click Open; log in when prompted.

Test the forwarding by typing xclock & on the server — a clock window must appear on your PC. (Built-in alternative on modern Windows: ssh -X user@host in PowerShell with an X server running.)

3Map your server home folder as a network drive (optional)

In Windows File Explorer, right-click This PC → Map network drive:

Enter the file-server path given by your college (VT's was \\filebox.ece.vt.edu), choose a free drive letter, and give your credentials:

4Copy files with WinSCP

Install WinSCP, choose the saved PuTTY session (or type host, user, password), and click Login. Drag files between the two panes. Remember to save Verilog/Tcl files with their real extensions, not .txt.

macOS: install XQuartz, open Terminal, and run ssh -X your_user@server.

8.2

Compile libraries and simulate with VCS/DVE

Why this stepThe Synopsys counterpart of Chapter 1 — useful when reading the original course.

The Synopsys version of Chapter 1. These tools are not on your VM; this is the course's procedure for reference.

1Compile the Liberty libraries to .db

Synopsys tools read libraries in their binary .db format. In the project directory, start Library Compiler and convert each .lib (the course compiles a standard-cell and an I/O-pad library):

Library Compiler (lc_shell) · shelllc_shell
#   read_lib ./libs/tcbn65gplusbc0d88.lib
#   write_lib tcbn65gplusbc0d88 -format db -output ./libs/tcbn65gplusbc0d88.db
#   read_lib ./libs/tpdn65gpgv2od3_sdbc.lib
#   write_lib tpdn65gpgv2od3_sdbc -format db -output ./libs/tpdn65gpgv2od3_sdbc.db
#   quit

2Compile and run with VCS

Course commands · shellvcs -full64 cnt_updown.v tb_cnt_updown.v
./simv
dve &

vcs compiles both files into an executable named simv (-full64 selects the 64-bit binaries):

Running ./simv executes the simulation and writes updown_counter.dump. Then start DVE (Discovery Visualization Environment):

3Open the dump in DVE

File → Open Database → select updown_counter.dump → Open:

The hierarchy appears once the database is loaded:

4Select signals and view waves

Click tb_cnt_updown in the hierarchy pane; its signals are listed in the variable pane:

Select them, then Signal → Add To Waves → New Wave View:

Finally View → Zoom → Zoom Full to see the whole run, and verify the same behavior table as Step 1.8:

8.3

Synthesize in Design Vision / dc_shell

Why this stepThe Synopsys counterpart of Chapter 2 — its outputs are what the course imports into Encounter.

The Synopsys version of Chapter 2. Start design_vision from the project directory (it reads .synopsys_dc.setup from there).

1Read the design

File → Read → select cnt_updown.v (set file type to All Files (*) if it is not listed) → Open.

2Look at the schematic

Select the design in the Logical Hierarchy window and click the Create Schematic button (second symbol on the toolbar):

A symbol for the block appears:

Double-click the symbol to see the generic logic inside it:

3Analyze, elaborate and link

  1. File → Analyze… → Add cnt_updown.v → Work Library WORK → tick Create new library if it does not exist → OK.
  2. File → Elaborate → Library WORK → OK.
  3. File → Link Design → add your ./libs/ path to the search path, make sure the compiled .db files are in the link library list → OK.

4Constraints and uniquify

Select the design → Hierarchy → Uniquify → OK (gives every instance of a repeated module its own copy so each can be optimized separately):

Load the constraints with File → Execute Script → file type All files (*) → cnt_updown.sdc → OK (or type source cnt_updown.sdc in the console):

5Compile, propagate activity, report and write

Run Design → Compile Ultra, tick Retime and Exact Map, OK, then propagate switching activity, report power and write the mapped Verilog. The activity commands used in the course:

Activity and automation · Tclwrite_saif -output ./cnt_updown_dv_prop.saif -propagated
read_saif -input ./cnt_updown_dv_prop.saif -instance updown_counter
report_power
write -format verilog -hierarchy -output cnt_updown_dve.v
write_sdc cnt_updown_syn.sdc
source dc_shell.tcl

Batch form: the course's dc_shell.tcl contains all of the above as commands; run it with dc_shell -f dc_shell.tcl | tee dc.log. Its outputs (cnt_updown_dve.v and cnt_updown_syn.sdc) are what the course imports into Encounter in Step 4.2.

REFERENCE

Glossary

Every abbreviation used on this page, in one place. Type in the box to filter.
TERMMEANING
Electrical effort hCout/Cin of a gate — its fan-out ratio.
Parasitic delay pDelay of a gate charging its own output capacitance, independent of load.
Stage effort ff = g·h, the load-dependent part of a gate’s delay.
Branching effort b, B(Con-path + Coff-path)/Con-path at a node; B is the product along a path.
Path effort FF = G·B·H, fixed for a path; minimum delay N·F1/N + P.
Arrival / required timeLatest time a signal can change at a pin / latest time it may arrive and still be captured.
Critical pathThe path with the smallest slack — it limits the clock frequency.
NLDMNon-linear delay model: Liberty tables of delay vs input slew and output load.
Elmore delayΣ Rk·Cdownstream along a path in an RC tree.
Generate / propagateg = a·b, p = a ⊕ b: the building blocks of fast adders.
Parallel prefix adderAdder computing all carries with an associative (G,P) operator in log₂n levels (e.g. Kogge–Stone).
Domino logicDynamic precharge/evaluate gates followed by inverters.
Charge sharingLoss of voltage on a dynamic node when it connects to discharged internal capacitance.
Time borrowingLate data passing through a transparent latch, using time from the next stage.
Latch-upParasitic PNPN thyristor turning on and shorting VDD to VSS.
Well tap / end capCells tying wells and substrate to the supplies / closing row ends.
JitterVariation in the timing of clock edges themselves.
CPPRCommon path pessimism removal — gives back OCV derating on the shared clock path.
Body effectThreshold rises when the source is above the body: Vt = Vt0 + γ(√(2φF+VSB) − √(2φF)).
BDDBinary decision diagram — a canonical graph form of a Boolean function for a fixed variable order.
D-algorithmATPG method using values {0,1,X,D,D̄} to activate and propagate a fault.
Dennard scalingConstant-field scaling: dimensions and voltage shrink together, keeping power density constant.
EDP / PDPEnergy–delay product / power–delay product (energy per switching event).
Equivalence checking (LEC)Formal proof that two netlists compute the same functions, via a miter f ⊕ g.
Prime implicantA product term covering only 1s of a function that cannot be enlarged further.
Pelgrom’s lawσ(ΔVt) = AVt/√(WL): mismatch shrinks with device area.
AOCVAdvanced OCV — derates that depend on path depth and distance.
Lee algorithmBreadth-first maze routing that always finds a shortest grid path.
Steiner treeMinimum-length tree connecting pins, allowed extra branching points.
RetimingMoving registers across logic without changing function.
Useful skewDeliberately unequal clock arrival times chosen to improve timing.
Transition faultAt-speed fault model: a node is slow to rise or slow to fall.
Antenna effectPlasma charging of gate oxide through long metal during fabrication.
Sheet resistanceR□ = ρ/t — resistance per square of a layer.
Transmission gateParallel NMOS + PMOS switch that passes both 0 and 1 fully.
CMOSComplementary MOS — logic built from paired NMOS pull-down and PMOS pull-up networks.
Noise marginHow much noise a logic level tolerates: NML = VIL − VOL, NMH = VOH − VIH.
Logical effortRatio of a gate’s input capacitance to an inverter’s delivering the same current (g).
FO4Delay of an inverter driving four copies of itself — a technology-independent delay unit.
LatchLevel-sensitive storage element; transparent while enabled.
MetastabilityA flop output hanging between 0 and 1 after a setup/hold violation.
MTBFMean time between failures (here: of a synchroniser).
LFSRLinear feedback shift register — generates pseudo-random patterns.
MISR / BISTMultiple-input signature register / built-in self-test.
Rent’s ruleT = t·Gp: pins of a block grow as a power of its gate count.
DecapOn-chip capacitor between VDD and VSS that supplies charge locally.
Threshold voltage VtGate voltage at which a MOSFET channel starts to conduct.
Velocity saturationShort-channel effect making ID ∝ (VGS − Vt)α with α ≈ 1.3.
Recovery / removalSetup/hold-like timing checks on asynchronous reset pins.
ASICApplication-Specific Integrated Circuit — a chip designed for one purpose.
ATPGAutomatic Test Pattern Generation — computes scan test patterns (Ch 6).
CTSClock Tree Synthesis — builds the buffered clock network (Step 4.12).
DEFDesign Exchange Format — the placed/routed layout in text form.
DFTDesign For Test — hardware added so chips can be tested after manufacture.
DRCDesign Rule Check — geometry obeys the foundry rules.
DRVDesign Rule Violation (electrical) — max transition, max capacitance, max fanout.
DUTDevice Under Test — the design instantiated inside a testbench.
ElaborationBuilding the full design hierarchy from analysed modules.
EMElectromigration — wire wear-out from high current density.
Filler cellEmpty cell that keeps wells and rails continuous between real cells.
Follow pinsThe VDD/VSS rails along each standard-cell row (Metal1).
GDSIIBinary polygon format sent to the foundry.
GcellA tile of the global-routing grid.
Hold timeHow long data must stay stable after the clock edge.
HPWLHalf-perimeter wire length — the placer’s wire-length estimate.
IR dropSupply voltage lost across power-grid resistance.
LatencyClock delay from the clock source to a flop.
LEFLibrary Exchange Format — cell outlines/pins and metal-layer rules.
Liberty (.lib)Cell timing, power and function tables.
LVSLayout Versus Schematic — layout extracts to the same circuit as the netlist.
MMMCMulti-Mode Multi-Corner — set of analysis views (modes × corners).
NetlistList of cell instances and the nets connecting them.
OCVOn-Chip Variation — pessimism for differences across one die.
PDKProcess Design Kit — all foundry data for one technology.
PVTProcess, Voltage, Temperature — the axes of timing corners.
QRCCadence parasitic extraction technology (tech file used by Encounter).
RTLRegister-Transfer Level — Verilog describing registers and logic between them.
Scan chainFlops linked into a shift register in test mode.
SDCSynopsys Design Constraints — clocks, I/O delays, exceptions.
SDFStandard Delay Format — computed delays for timing simulation.
SE / SI / SOScan enable / scan in / scan out.
Setup timeHow long data must be stable before the clock edge.
SISignal integrity — crosstalk effects between neighbouring wires (also “scan in” in Ch 6).
SkewDifference in clock arrival between two flops.
SlackRequired time − arrival time. Negative means a violation.
SnapshotAn elaborated, ready-to-run simulation image (NC tools).
SPEFStandard Parasitic Exchange Format — extracted R and C per net.
STAStatic Timing Analysis — exhaustive path-based timing check.
StripeWide power wire crossing the core, connected to the ring.
TCFToggle Count Format — per-net switching activity.
Tie cellCell that outputs a constant 1 or 0 safely.
UtilizationCell area ÷ core area.
VCDValue Change Dump — text waveform file.
WNS / TNSWorst / Total Negative Slack — summary of all violations.
